chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

The pebbles for throwing at the Jamarat should be like the size of a fingernail. Do not take them black, white, or red; take them dark-colored and speckled. Throw them with a casual throw, place them on the thumb, and push them off with the nail of the index finger.

He said: Throw them from the middle of the valley, and keep all of them on your right side. Do not throw at the top of the Jamarah. You stand at the first two Jamarat, and do not stand at the Jamarat al-Aqabah.
It is appropriate that you pick up the pebbles and do not break any of them. This was narrated.

key_terms.جَمْرَة الْعَقَبَة: The Jamarat al-Aqabah (the first and largest pillar)
key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: Pebbles used for throwing at the Jamarat

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rules for selecting and throwing pebbles during the Hajj ritual of Rami al-Jamarat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides precise juristic details for Rami al-Jamarat, emphasizing the selection of small, speckled pebbles (kuhlīyyah) and the specific technique of throwing from the valley floor. It distinguishes the ritual by mandating standing (wuqūf) only at the first two Jamarat pillars, excluding the Jamarat al-Aqabah, which reflects the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' specific practices during the Hajj pilgrimage.
